summary: All four first-pass findings are real and correctly filed as minor. None is suspicious and none has the wrong severity. The overall approach holds up: a form POST answered by a 303 back to a GET page, one row per vote in a single table, counts worked out on each read, and the tally on the owner-only admin page. Sketching the slice independently gives the same structure, and each place the design differs from that sketch has a reason in the tree: TestReaderPagesShareOneLayout, the form-action rule, and the measured BUSY results from the spike. Two minor items were missed. First, the CC-001 check stopped at one of the three new rules. Rule 2 does not catch a comma join or `UPDATE OR <conflict> votes`. Rule 3 does not catch SAVEPOINT, which in SQLite starts the same deferred transaction the spike measured failing, and it does not catch a lowercase `begin`. Second, several key decisions depend on what test_e003_1 contains, but the design records none of those facts as a sourced claim. The first reviewer said in prose that it could not check them but filed no finding. The most important of these is where the finish-line test looks for the author's dislike count.

assessments.note: Correct, and filed at the right severity. The case 'show dislikes only to the author' lists the owner as an observer of /admin/reports/x only. So a count rendered under {{if .Viewer.IsOwner}} in report.html would leave every non-owner observation unchanged, and both token rules would stay quiet. Rule 1's because text claims the test catches exactly this hole. The gap matters more than it first looks: the design dropped practice's in-tree keyword scan on the grounds that the finish-line test's beside() already scans. That test is not in the tree (lesson #928), so for later slices TestDislikesDoNotInterfere is the only in-tree guard. The fix is cheap and keeps the test deterministic: the owner casts nothing between the two recordings, and Public counts only kind='up'. It is minor because nothing leaks at ship. The gap is in protecting against a future edit.

Real, and minor is right. The design marks this invariant must-verify, but nothing makes it hold. Two corrections to how it was filed. (a) 'Already false today' is true but harmless: /raw, /healthz, /static and /auth/* do not read votes, so leaving them out is not a breach of what the invariant protects. (b) The proposed publicRoutes table only covers new routes automatically if registering a route inline in router.go is also forbidden, for example by a fitness rule that mux.HandleFunc/Handle appear only in the loop over the table. Without that, a later slice can still register outside the table, and the 'remember to add it' problem just moves. The vote POST also needs a body, so a plain loop over the table cannot observe it without a per-row request builder. Deferring it to the show-all or comments slice, as the finding allows, is acceptable.

Correct. Selection rationale (2) says the handler 'cannot read ViewerFrom and forget the error'. That holds only by convention, because ViewerFrom stays exported for later code. The proposed token fence follows the same reasoning the design uses for its own OwnerTally fence, and matches the house idiom (BySlug/ListAll, OpenRaw). The exceptions are right: reader.go deliberately treats a failed lookup as anonymous, and admin.go:60 already calls ViewerFrom. Nothing in this slice misbehaves, so minor.

Correct under CC-001. A quoted identifier, a schema-qualified name (main.votes), and a VIEW or trigger in a later .sql migration (outside the **/*.go glob) all get past rule 2 without the bare token appearing in Go. Naming these in bounded_by rather than chasing every spelling follows #939. The pass is incomplete for rule 2 itself, though (a comma join and UPDATE OR <conflict>), and it never looked at rule 3. Both are filed under missed.

missed.claim: The CC-001 check was applied only to rule 2's quoting and view holes. Plain uppercase SQL still gets past two of the three new rules. Rule 2 (`\b(FROM|INTO|UPDATE|JOIN)\s+votes\b`) misses a comma join, `SELECT ... FROM reports r, votes v WHERE ...`. That is the likely shape of a ranking query that a show-all page outside internal/votes would write, and it is the m2 leak scenario. Rule 2 also misses `UPDATE OR IGNORE votes` and `UPDATE OR REPLACE votes`. Rule 3 (`\.Begin(Tx)?\(`, `\bBEGIN\b`) misses `SAVEPOINT s; SELECT ...; UPDATE ...; RELEASE s` on a db.Conn. In SQLite's autocommit mode, SAVEPOINT starts a DEFERRED transaction, which is exactly the read-then-write upgrade the spike measured failing. Rule 3 also misses a lowercase `begin`, and its because text names no known hole, which the design's own Fitness component requires (#939).
missed.evidence: Design architecture_rules, rule 2 and rule 3 must_not_match patterns. The 'Fitness rules and corpus rows' component requires a bounded_by entry for each rule. SQLite's SAVEPOINT documentation says a SAVEPOINT issued outside a transaction begins a standard autocommit BEGIN DEFERRED TRANSACTION. Spike concurrent-vote-upserts-no-busy measured 215-253 BUSY/BUSY_SNAPSHOT errors per run for the deferred change-vote, with lost rows. CC-001 asks reviewers to check equivalent mechanisms.
missed.fix: Rule 3: change must_not_match to `(?i)\b(BEGIN|SAVEPOINT)\b` alongside `\.Begin(Tx)?\(`. The rule is scoped to internal/votes, so the cost of case-insensitive matching on comments stays inside one small package. Add fire rows for SAVEPOINT and for lowercase begin. Rule 2: add `\bUPDATE\s+OR\s+[A-Z]+\s+votes\b` to must_not_match. Do not add a bare `,\s*votes\b` pattern, because it fires on Go argument lists such as `f(w, votes)`. Instead, name comma joins in bounded_by next to m4's additions, with a known-quiet row so whoever closes the hole later can flip it to fire.

missed.claim: Premortem: the slice reaches the build or validate stage, test_e003_1 looks for the author's dislike count somewhere the design did not put it, and the privacy architecture has to be reopened after the build. Several key choices depend on the content of the finish-line test, which is not in the tree. The design records none of those facts as a code_claim or outside_claim with a source, so neither the critique nor this pass could check them. (a) The in-tree keyword leak scan was dropped because 'the scan already lives in the finish-line test's beside()'. (b) The second sign-in anchor was dropped to keep 'the acceptance test's links[0]' untouched. (c) The owner's dislike count goes only on /admin/reports/<slug>, 'each number in its label's block'. If the test expects the author to see the count on /reports/<slug>, the whole PublicView-has-no-dislike-field decision must be reopened, not just the markup. (d) The like-count selector, the button labels 'Thumbs up', 'Thumbs down' and 'Take back my vote', the expected behaviour for an anonymous POST, and 'withdraws after a switch and again later'. Design-slice is the stage that should have recorded these, citing the E-003 epic row it read.
missed.evidence: Design selection_rationale (3) and (7); key_interactions of the 'Reader page votes block' and 'Tests' components; the contract auth_model ('the finish-line test sends one only if the page has one'). code_claims has no entry for tests/acceptance or the E-003 epic, and outside_claims has none either. Critique reviews#681: 'I could not check the finish-line test test_e003_1. It is not in the tree (lesson #928) ... I have not verified ... where it looks for the owner's dislike count.' Q-005 shows acceptance bodies are stored only as ledger epic rows.
missed.fix: Record each test_e003_1 fact the design depends on as a claim sourced to the E-003 epic row in the ledger, so that a read-only SELECT can settle it. Build-slice must confirm (c) before writing the admin tally, and must run test_e003_1 locally as the design already requires. If (c) turns out wrong, send the slice back to design-slice instead of adding an IsOwner branch to report.html, which is the exact hole m1 describes.

payload.notes: The first reviewer was accurate and conservative. All four findings are minor, each is backed by evidence from the design, and none overreaches. It checked the seams the synthesis introduced (the '#votes' fragment against LocalPath, RowsAffected on UPSERT, the parse rule for INSERT…SELECT…ON CONFLICT), and those hold. Two patterns are worth noting. (1) It applied CC-001 to only one of the three new fitness rules, and only to quoting and views, not to plain-SQL spellings or the SAVEPOINT mechanism. (2) It identified a load-bearing check it could not run (the contents of test_e003_1) but left it in prose instead of filing it, so it was not in the set anyone would act on. The synthesis seams that triggered this second review also check out: Participant's ErrSignedOut feeds the 303 back to the report, the shared-layout invariant forces the vote form to be the same on every page, and the determinism conditions of the noninterference test hold. Re-derivation deltas I considered and did not file: the choice to make a failed vote read return 503 for the whole reader page instead of omitting the votes block (a conservative judgment that rarely triggers, since the report row was just read from the same pool); and the case where Withdraw runs after a report was unpublished between the lookup and the write, which answers 303 instead of the contract's 404 (harmless, because only the reader's own row changes and the Location is the same for every outcome).
